root.name: Pterodactyl Defense: Western, Anhanguera
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nf3 c5 4. Be3 Qa5+

overview: Black plays ...g6, ...Bg7 and ...c5 and puts the queen on a5 with check against the e3 bishop, an early-queen hypermodern idea. White can reply with Bd2, Nbd2 or c3 and a centre with dxc5, aiming for a space advantage, while Black tries to exploit the half-open c-file and the pin on the e-file. Play is unusual and tactical, with Black's queen sometimes hunted.

white_ideas.idea: Build a pawn centre with c3, Nbd2 and e5 ideas
Chase the queen with Bd2 or Nbd2 and take space
Capture on c5 and use the extra development

black_ideas.idea: Hit the centre with ...c5 and ...cxd4 and use the long diagonal
Keep the queen active on a5
Counterattack e4 and the d4 pawn

typical_structures.structure: Hypermodern Sicilian-style structure with Black fianchetto and open c-file
Maroczy-like bind if White plays c4

character.notes: Unusual and tactical; the early queen means mistakes are punished.

gambit.notes: The d4 pawn is usually regained, so no gambit in the main lines.

soundness.notes: Sound but risky; White has a comfortable game with accurate play.

structure.notes: Asymmetric Sicilian-style centre with the c-file half open.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players; it is mainly a surprise weapon.

level.notes: The early queen needs careful handling.

sublines_that_differ.name: Rhamphorhynchus
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 g6 3. d4 Bg7 4. dxc5 Qa5+
sublines_that_differ.how: White takes on c5 and Black regains the pawn with ...Qxc5.

character.reason: An early queen on a5 makes the play double-edged.

gambit.reason: No gambit in the main lines.

structure.reason: Sicilian-style asymmetry with a half-open c-file.

plans.reason: The early queen and the g7 bishop are the main ideas.
